title: India’s Voter Roll Revision: What Is SIR and Why Is It Controversial?

ai.summary: India's voter roll revision process, known as SIR, is controversial as it requires voters to link themselves or a parent to the roll from their state's last revision two decades ago.

facts.claim: voters must link themselves, or a parent, to the roll from their state's last such revision two decades ago
facts.quote: the Special Intensive Revision is the Election Commission's house-to-house recheck of India's voter lists. Voters must link themselves, or a parent, to the roll from their state's last such revision two decades ago.

ai.background_note: The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is the Election Commission's house-to-house recheck of India's voter lists, requiring voters to link themselves or a parent to the roll from their state's last revision two decades ago.
